name: Brown Heart
tldr: Earthy love! Nature, diversity, or comfort.

contextMeanings.meaning: Used for diversity and POC pride.

platformNotes.note: Diversity and POC-pride posts use 🤎 as a literal skin-tone-coded heart; also reads as autumn-coded.
Staple of fall aesthetic and 'clean girl' brown-toned posts; pairs with 🍂 and ☕.
Cozy and earthy content default; reads as 'grounded warmth' rather than romance.
Less loaded than other hearts in most servers; appears in cozy-mood channels.

seoDescription: Learn what the Brown Heart emoji 🤎 really means.

longForm.overview:
The 🤎 brown heart was added in Unicode 12 (2019) and quickly split into two parallel meanings. The first is aesthetic: brown-coded fall content, cozy vibes, and 'clean girl' neutral palettes where 🤎 pairs with cream and tan. The second is identity-coded: Brown pride, POC visibility, and skin-tone representation in a heart that had historically defaulted to lighter pinks. In 2026 both readings are mainstream, and which one a sender activates depends on the surrounding text.

In real-world chat 🤎 lives in a warm, grounded register. It is not the strongest heart (that is ❤️), not the friendship heart (💛), not the romance heart. It is the 'I am cozy with you' heart — useful for content about comfort, autumn, coffee, and identity. Writers should pick 🤎 when they want warmth without romantic weight and when the context allows the earthy or POC-pride read.
longForm.howPeopleUseIt:
🤎 shows up at the end of fall aesthetic posts, in POC-pride captions, and in cozy-mood content of every kind. People send it after a coffee run, a hike in autumn woods, or a friend's announcement about heritage. The emoji pairs naturally with 🍂 for autumn content, ☕ for coffee culture, and 🤎🫶 for the brown heart with hands.

In dating contexts 🤎 can read as 'I am grounded with you' — a softer romantic signal than ❤️. In family chats 🤎 is the warm, all-ages-appropriate heart when the topic is comfort food or home.
longForm.whenNotToUse:
Skip 🤎 in a romantic context where the partner expects ❤️. Sending 🤎 where ❤️ would land can read as 'cozy, not romantic,' which may not match the sender's intent. Avoid it in any context where the recipient expects a clear romantic signal and will read brown as 'I am warm but I do not love you.'

Also avoid 🤎 in ironic or dark contexts — the color reads as earnest and cozy, so sarcasm with 🤎 lands flat.
longForm.howToReply:
Mirror 🤎 with another 🤎 if you want to keep the cozy register, or pair with 🍂 to amplify the autumn aesthetic. If the sender is signaling identity-coded pride, mirror with 🤎 and a sentence that affirms the read ('love that'). If the sender is using 🤎 as a soft romantic signal, mirror with 🤎 to keep the register or escalate to ❤️ if you want a stronger read.

If 🤎 lands in a POC-pride context and you want to engage, mirror with 🤎 and an affirming sentence. The color is doing identity work, not just aesthetic work.

faqs.question: What does 🤎 mean in text?
faqs.answer: 🤎 means either earthy/aesthetic warmth (autumn, coffee, cozy) or POC pride and diversity-coded affection. The read depends on context.

faqs.question: Is 🤎 flirty?
faqs.answer: 🤎 can read as soft-flirty in dating contexts — a 'grounded warmth' signal. In identity-coded contexts it is community love, not romantic.

faqs.question: What does 🤎 mean from a Black person?
faqs.answer: From a Black person, 🤎 often signals Brown pride or POC-coded affection — a heart that acknowledges skin tone rather than defaulting to pink.

faqs.question: What is the difference between 🤎 and ❤️?
faqs.answer: ❤️ is the strongest romantic heart; 🤎 is earthy warmth, aesthetic-coded, or identity-coded. The color matters for the read.
